Vs

full_judgment: 12. The appellant has been acquitted on the ground of benefit of doubt of the charge of theft under section 380, Penal Code. Since the Magistrate found some discrepancy in the evidence of the informant, and his wife about the person removing the trunk, he thought that the appellant was entitled to benefit of doubt. We refrain from commenting on the conclusion drawn by the Magistrate, but we proceed on the basic of this finding. The fact of acquittal of the appellant of the charge of theft under section 380 P.C. is, with regard to a totally distinct and separate offence from that under section 457 P.C. One is not dependent on the other. The failure of one does not lead to the failure of the other. The fact that the appellant has been found innocent of the charge of theft does not follow, that his entry was either innocent, or was not made with the intent to commit theft. He has offered no explanation of his presence in the house of the informant at the unearthly hours of the night. Failure to offer any reason able explanation cannot be ignored. Presumption can fairly be drawn of criminal intent. In the present case, circumstances are ample to lend support to the inference that his intention was to commit theft. The contention of Mr. Behatar Ali fails.
